name: @playliquid/lab-organization
description: PlayLiquid GameOS Lab organization compiler/search (PL-029). The organization-search stage of the Lab loop (spec/architecture.md §Lab loop): a TOTAL, deterministic compiler that turns lab-contracts organization descriptors into evaluation-ready compiled records — agent slots resolved against avatar-runtime body/capability surfaces (R5 restriction projection consumed, never duplicated), model assignments carried as opaque ZCode seam references, tools/memory topology/budget/scheduling/review structure carried as typed compiled records — with typed kebab-case rejections accumulated in one pass (never throws, never any). A typed, bounded candidate-space model over the architecture's twelve dimensions (agents, roles, bodies, model assignments, tools, capabilities, communication/delegation, memory topology, human participation, budget, scheduling, review structure): explicit enumerations, per-dimension caps and cross-product caps with typed out-of-space refusals — finite per request, no unbounded generation. Seeded deterministic search (E9): a search request (tenant, objective context, dimension bounds, seed) opens a cursorable stream of candidate organizations in a stable content-derived order — the generalist baseline (lock 26) is always candidate zero of the space — with typed non-monotonic cursor refusals. Evaluation wiring: candidates compile into lab-simulation evaluation requests and are scored by the deterministic PL-028 engine; results are immutable labeled estimates (E10/E11) recorded as tenant-scoped evidence, idempotent by content key (re-evaluation replays the recorded outcome). Capability gaps resolve through lab-contracts' frozen gap ladder (typed rungs; blocked is a typed terminal, never an exception) and are recorded as typed findings, never silently skipped. Pure domain: the service instance is the single mutable-state owner; time, body catalogs, tool catalogs, evaluation and persistence live behind ports with deterministic in-memory fakes; no real model assignment (ZCode is a host concern), no Arena escalation runtime, no network.
